details:
BEYOND is a first-person browser game in which players design and operate complete missions to the International Space Station or Moon. It connects mission planning, spacecraft operation, scientific work and recovery, allowing players to experience how engineering decisions affect an entire mission.

Players begin by choosing a destination, scientific payload, launch vehicle, equipment, and reserves. The planner checks mass, available power, budget, and launcher compatibility before allowing launch. These choices have consequences: additional batteries increase power capacity and stored energy but also add mass and cost. Different payloads change power demand, scientific output, and operating requirements.

During the mission, players operate physical cockpit controls, follow their trajectory, monitor resources, and complete docking or landing maneuvers. The ISS route includes entering the station and conducting research. The lunar route includes surface experiments, sample collection, and ascent. Equipment faults require decisions about recovery and remaining resources. Success requires completing the scientific objective and returning the crew and results safely to Earth. A debrief and exportable mission report support reviewing outcomes and trying another configuration.

The intended benefit is to make mission-design trade-offs easier to understand through experimentation. Students and space enthusiasts can connect concepts such as power capacity, payload mass, propulsion, and orbital motion to visible outcomes. Cadet, Commander, and Expert settings provide different levels of assistance and resource margins. Contextual explanations introduce relevant concepts during play. The intended impact is greater interest in space engineering and a better understanding of how interconnected systems influence mission success; learning outcomes still require classroom evaluation.

The game uses TypeScript, React, Vite, and Babylon.js, with WebGPU support and a WebGL fallback. Blender and Python scripts support asset preparation and modeling. Browser audio and speech synthesis provide effects and authored guidance. Open-Meteo supplies optional launch-site weather. Node-based checks and Playwright support automated validation. OpenAI Codex assisted with development, testing, modeling scripts, and documentation; the concept originated with the team, and no LLM runs during gameplay.
